item.text:
1. “modeled verbatim” conflates two distinct FGMN normalizations — justification gap.

> “the anchored-march identity:
> \[
> \operatorname{in}(f)=\phi_{w(f)}R^{gr}(\operatorname{in}f)(\bar y)
> \]
> ONE invertible anchor monomial…”

and

> “modeled verbatim on FGMN Thm 4.2:
> ‘\(H_\mu(g)=\phi_r(g)R_r(g)(y_r)\)’”

These are not verbatim-equivalent. The printed theorem distinguishes
\[
H_\mu(g)=\phi_r(\alpha)R_{r,\alpha}(g)(y_r)
       =\phi_r(g)R_r(g)(y_r),\qquad \alpha=\mu(g).
\]
The weight-indexed anchor \(\phi_r(\alpha)\) accompanies \(R_{r,\alpha}\); the ordinary residual \(R_r(g)\) accompanies the polynomial-dependent anchor \(\phi_r(g)\). REV 2 combines the weight-indexed anchor with the ordinary/GMN residual without proving that the difference is only a scalar. In general it can include a power of \(y_r\), determined by the side’s initial abscissa. The paper’s definitions explicitly distinguish \(R_{r,\alpha}\) from \(R_r\), and parameterize coefficients along \(s_r(\alpha)+je_r\). [FGMN paper text](https://diposit.ub.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/a62d4de6-7e36-41ee-8be9-8c4a3d000887/content)

This does not invalidate “GD3-FULL given (GR-B),” because (2′) explicitly assumes the stronger identity. It does invalidate the claims that (2′) is “modeled verbatim,” has already been pinned clause-for-clause, or differs from FGMN only by the three listed normalization caveats. The extra identification remains part of the open input.

2. Properness required by the cited faithfulness theorem is not established — justification gap.

> “every MacLane-chain key is proper … and the brief’s state key has
> \(\deg\Phi_{i+1}=e_i g_i\deg\Phi_i\), a multiple of \(e\cdot m\) — proper”

FGMN Proposition 5.14 expressly has different conclusions for proper and improper key polynomials; Corollary 5.15 gives the asserted exact order equality only for a proper key. The printed characterization is that a key is proper iff some MacLane chain ends with a key not equivalent to it—not merely because its degree is a multiple of the preceding degree. [FGMN Proposition 5.14 and Corollary 5.15](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=0915764dde26c2da6df40ef854806e27275c4ba0&repid=rep1&type=pdf)

Neither displayed `(KP)` nor the degree law contains the required non-equivalence/properness condition. Again, clause (GR-B)(4) explicitly assumes faithfulness, so Route B remains a valid conditional argument; its advertised derivation from Proposition 5.14/Corollary 5.15 does not yet meet the printed hypothesis.

Audit conclusions:

- Higher-order valuation composition: repaired successfully. `(KPirr)` supplies MacLane Def. 4.1(i), the `(KPa)` degree block supplies 4.1(ii), monicity supplies 4.1(iii), and \(\gamma_{i+1}>e_iw_i(\Phi_i)\) supplies the augmentation inequality. BRIDGE is used only under the valuation induction hypothesis. No missing irreducibility premise remains.
- Slot-twist repair: the anchored-march requirement appears at all necessary statement and consumption sites—GD-3 full/slot law, (GR-B)(2′), GD3-FULL/OL-B, IFACE(c), and the ledger. But its claimed exact match to FGMN is not verified because of the \(\phi_r(\alpha),R_{r,\alpha}\) versus \(\phi_r(g),R_r\) conflation above.
- Interface scope: honestly restricted. Clause (b) is confined to GMN’s scope; outside it only the intrinsic sheared \(w\)-polygon is claimed. Clauses (a) and (c) retain their separate conditional scopes. I find no surviving uniform-“any \(O\)” claim for the GMN polygon identification.

VERDICT: SOUND-WITH-GAPS
